summary.tldr: Bill C-231 would let youth justice officials use treatment program conditions and, in some cases, delay sentencing so a young person can attend treatment.
what_it_does: Requires police, in some drug or cannabis cases, to consider referring a young person to a problematic substance use treatment program, with the young person’s consent.
Allows an extrajudicial sanction, a response kept outside court, to require a young person to attend a problematic substance use treatment program or another treatment program.
Allows a youth justice court, with the consent of the Attorney General and the young person, to delay sentencing so the young person can attend treatment.
Lets a youth sentence order a young person to attend an approved non-residential program, including a treatment program, for up to 240 hours over no more than six months.
Adds treatment program attendance as a possible condition in certain orders and in conditional supervision orders.
who_it_affects: Young people in the youth justice system
Young people charged with drug or cannabis offences
summary.background: The bill amends the Youth Criminal Justice Act. It also includes a coordinating amendment that would apply if Bill C-16 becomes law.
